Freed and free-born Black Americans, and their descendants, who settled the West African coast from 1822 and founded Liberia. The American Colonization Society, a group of white Americans who wanted free Black people to leave the United States, paid for the first ships to Cape Mesurado, where Monrovia grew.

Liberia declared independence in 1847 under Joseph Jenkins Roberts. The settlers were a small share of the population but held power. They built churches, houses and a political culture modelled on the American South, and kept the local African peoples out of power for generations.

The True Whig Party ruled without a break from 1878. That ended in 1980, when Samuel Doe, an army sergeant from an indigenous group, seized power and killed President William Tolbert. The coup was followed by years of civil war.
